Rashi on Eruvin 23a:10:1.english: With arkablin - The name of a bitter herb.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:10:2.hebrew: ובקשתי לי חבר - לשלשה דברים הללו, אם שמען מפיו, ולא מצאתי. ובגמרא מפרש: דגבי גינה וקרפף לא שרו יותר מבית סאתים, וגבי אנשי חצר סברי דאף להם אסור ביתו, אבל מבתיהן לחצר מותר — ובגמ' מפרש פלוגתייהו — ובערקבלין סברי דלאו מרור הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:10:2.english: And I sought for myself a colleague - For these three matters, [to see] whether [anyone else] had heard them from his mouth; and I did not find [one]. And in the Gemara it explains: that regarding a garden and an enclosure, they did not permit more than a beit se'atayim; and regarding the residents of a courtyard, they hold that his house is forbidden even to them, but [carrying] from their houses into the courtyard is permitted — and in the Gemara [it will] explain their dispute — and regarding arkablin, they hold that it is not bitter herbs.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:11:1.english: Which Tanna [is referred to] - Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava in [the case of] the garden and karpef above.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:11:2.english: That it says: “And furthermore” - Which implies that he stated another stringency regarding it earlier.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:12:1.hebrew: אילימא משום דאמר חדא לחומרא - גבי פסין, דאמר דאין עושין אותן אלא לבאר הרבים; והשתא קאמר חומרא אחריתי, דאע"ג דהוקף לדירה לא שרי טפי מבית סאתים:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:12:1.english: If you say [it is] because he stated one stringency - Regarding the upright boards [around a well], where he said that they may be made only for a public well; and now he states another stringency, that even though it was enclosed for habitation, it is not permitted [if it is] larger than two beit se'ah.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:12:2.hebrew: והא רבי יהודה בר אלעאי דתנא לעיל חדא לחומרא - דאמר: ״עד בית סאתים״ — אין, טפי — לא, והדר תנא אחריתי: ״יסלקנה לצדדין״, ולא תנא ״ועוד״ — משום דלאו בחדא מלתא היא, דרישא איירי במדת היקף, וסיפא איירי בביטול מחיצות:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:12:2.english: And didn't Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai teach above one stringency - For he said: Up to two beit se’a — yes; more [than that] — no. And then he taught another [stringency]: "He should divert it to the sides." And [yet the tanna] did not teach "And furthermore" — because they are not concerning a single matter, as the first clause deals with the dimensions of the enclosure, and the latter clause deals with the nullification of partitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:13:1.hebrew: אפסקוה רבנן - דקא תני: ״אמרו לו: לא אמרו בית סאתים אלא לגינה כו'״:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:13:1.english: The Rabbis interrupted him - As [the mishna] teaches: "They said to him: 'They only said [an area of] two beit se'ah for a garden, etc.'"

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:14:1.hebrew: וכל היכא דאפסקוה רבנן לא הוה תני בה ועוד - אי שייך למימר בה, כגון היכא דרישא וסיפא בחדא מילתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:14:1.english: And wherever the Rabbis interrupted him, would [the tanna] not teach "and furthermore" in it? - [Even] where it is applicable to say so in it, such as where the first clause and the final clause are on one [and the same] matter.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:14:2.hebrew: והא ר' אליעזר דסוכה - דתנן במסכת (סוכה ד' כז.): ר' אליעזר אומר: י"ד סעודות חייב אדם לאכול בסוכה, וחכמים אומרים: אין לדבר קצבה. ועוד אמר ר' אליעזר: מי שלא אכל לילי יו"ט הראשון, ישלים לילי יום טוב האחרון. אלמא, משום דרישא וסיפא בסעודה דסוכה ובחשבונן איירי, תנא ועוד, אע"ג דאפסקוה. ושמע מינה: האי דלא תנא בדרבי יהודה ועוד — משום דלא דמי הוא; ובדרבי יהודה בן בבא — למה לי דתני ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:14:2.english: But Rabbi Eliezer of Sukkah - As we learned in a mishna in tractate Sukkah (27a): "Rabbi Eliezer says: A person is obligated to eat fourteen meals in the sukkah, and the Sages say: There is no fixed quota for the matter. And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said: Whoever did not eat on the first night of the Festival shall make it up on the last night of the Festival." Evidently, because both the beginning and the end [of his statements] deal with the meal of the sukkah and their count, the tanna taught "And furthermore," even though [the Rabbis] interrupted him. And deduce from this: That which [the tanna] did not teach "And furthermore" in [the case of] Rabbi Yehuda is because [the two cases] are not similar [to each other]; and in [the case of] Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, why did [the tanna] need to teach it?

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:15:1.hebrew: התם - גבי סוכה, במלתיה אפסקוה — לא אהדרו ליה רבנן אלא בסעודות. אבל רבי יהודה דמתני' לא איירי אלא בפסי ביראות בית סאתים, ואהדרו רבנן בגינה וקרפף ודיר וסהר. ולעולם טעמיה משום הפסקה; ולר' יהודה בן בבא דלא אפסקיה, תנא ועוד:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:15:1.english: There - In the case of *Sukka*, they interrupted him regarding his [own] matter — the Rabbis responded to him only concerning meals. However, Rabbi Yehuda of our mishna was speaking only about well-strips [of] two *beit se’a*, and the Rabbis responded regarding a garden, an enclosure, a pen, and a fold. And indeed, the reason is because of an interruption; and regarding Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, whom they did not interrupt, [the *tanna*] taught: “And furthermore.”

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:2:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא דרבים אפי' מכונסין - שרי ר"י בן בבא. והאי דקאמר באר הרבים — משום ר' עקיבא, דאמר: באר היחיד שרי; ואתא איהו למימר: אע"ג דמים חיים נינהו, דרבים — אין, דיחיד — לא. והכי קאמר: אין עושין פסין אפילו לבאר, אלא של רבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:2:1.english: I would have said: [Water] of the public, even collected - Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava permits [it]. And that which he said, "a public well," [was] because of Rabbi Akiva, who said [that] a private well is permitted; and he came to say [that] even though it is living water, [a well] of the public — yes; [a well] of an individual — no. And this is what he is saying: One does not make upright boards even for a well, unless [it is] of the public.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:5:1.hebrew: שומירה - סוכת שומרין. ואע"ג דהוקף לדירה, בית סאתים הוא דשרי, טפי לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:5:1.english: A watchman's booth - A booth for watchmen. And even though it was enclosed for dwelling, it is [only] a beit se'atayim that is permitted; more [than that is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:5:2.hebrew: סמוכה לעיר - דהואיל וקרובה לביתו, דעתו להשתמש בה תמיד, וכהוקף לדירה דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:5:2.english: Near the town - For since it is close to his house, he intends to use it constantly, and it is considered like [an area] enclosed for dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:6:1.hebrew: ובלבד שתהא שבעים אמה ושיריים על שבעים אמה ושיריים - ולא יותר. ובגמרא פריך: תנא קמא נמי הכי קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:6:1.english: Provided that it is seventy cubits and a remainder by seventy cubits and a remainder - And not more. And in the Gemara it asks: Doesn't the First Tanna also say this?

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:7:1.hebrew: אם היה ארכה יותר על רחבה אפילו אמה אחת - אע"ג דמיעט רחבה והוסיף בארכה, ואין בכולה אלא בית סאתים — אין מטלטלין, דמרובע הוא דשרו רבנן היכא דלא הוקף לדירה:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:7:1.english: If its length was greater than its breadth, even by one cubit - Even though one reduced its breadth and increased its length, and in its entirety there is only two beit se’ah — one may not carry [inside it], for it is [only a] square that the Sages permitted where it was not enclosed for dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:9:1.hebrew: אנשי חצר ששכח כו' - ולמחר ביטל רשותו לחברו, שהיא אוסרת עליהן מלהוציא מבתיהן לחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 23a:9:1.english: Residents of a courtyard, one of whom forgot, etc. - And on the next day [on Shabbat], he renounced his domain to his fellow [resident], which [otherwise] prohibits them from carrying out from their houses into the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:9:2.english: [As for] his house, it is forbidden to bring in and take out - [To and from] the courtyard, for his own need.

Rashi on Eruvin 23a:9:3.english: However, it is permitted to them - To bring the utensils of their houses into his house via the courtyard.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:12:1.hebrew: אילימא משום דתני חדא לחומרא - פירוש: דשייך למיתני "ועוד" אע"ג דלא הוו תרוייהו מענין א'; וכ"ש היכא דהוו תרוייהו מענין א', אף על גב דלא הוו תרוייהו לחומרא — כמו בסוכה (דף כז.) ובפרק רביעי דמגילה (דף כח.), כדפ"ה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:12:1.english: "If you say that because he taught one stringency" - The explanation is that it is appropriate to teach "And furthermore" even though they are not both on the same subject; and all the more so where they are both on the same subject, even though they are not both stringencies — as in Sukkah (27a) and in the fourth chapter of Megillah (28a), as Rashi explained.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:15:1.hebrew: הכא במלתא אחריתי אפסקוה - תימה: דבפרק המביא כדי יין (ביצה דף לד. ושם) קתני "ועוד", ואע"ג דאפסיק במילתא אחריתי — דקתני: "ר' אליעזר אומר: נוטל אדם קיסם משלפניו [לחצוץ בו שיניו] ומגבב מן החצר ומדליק, וחכ"א: מגבב משלפניו ומדליק", וקתני בתר הכי: "אין מוציאין את האור לא מן העצים כו'", ומפסיק בבא שלימה; וקתני בתר הכי: "ועוד א"ר אליעזר: עומד אדם על המוקצה כו'". ומיהו רש"י מהפך שם המשנה והגמ'. אך לר"ת, שאומר שאין צריך להפך, דמילתא דאור קא מסיים ואזיל — קשה. וי"ל: דהתם הוו תרי קולי, ושייך למיתני "ועוד" אע"ג דאפסיק במילתא אחריתי, דכח דהיתירא עדיף:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:15:1.english: "Here, they interrupted [him] with a different matter" - It is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "HaMevi Kadei Yayin" (Beitzah 34a and there), [the Mishnah] teaches "And furthermore," even though it was interrupted by a different matter — for it teaches: "Rabbi Eliezer says: A person may take a splinter from before him [to pick his teeth with it], and gather from the courtyard and kindle [a fire]; and the Sages say: He may gather [only] from before him and kindle [it]." And it teaches after this: "One may not produce fire, not from wood, etc.," and an entire clause interrupts [between them]; and it teaches after this: "And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said: A person may stand by the muktzeh, etc." However, Rashi reverses the order of the Mishnah and the Gemara there. Yet according to Rabbeinu Tam, who says that there is no need to reverse [the text], because [the Tanna] is continuing [in order] to conclude the topic of fire — it is difficult. And it can be answered that there, they were two leniencies, and it is fitting to teach "And furthermore" even though it was interrupted by a different matter, because the power of leniency is preferable.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:3:1.hebrew: והא דנקט באר הרבים לאפוקי מר' עקיבא - וא"ת: א"כ, הוה ליה למימר בור הרבים, וע"כ באר היחיד לא — דא"כ, היינו רבי עקיבא. וי"ל: דאורחא דמלתא למיתני מענין שממעט, דהיינו באר היחיד. אי נמי: הא דקאמר דרבים אפילו מכונסין — לאו אר"י בן בבא קאי, אלא אשמואל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:3:1.english: "And that which [the Mishnah] stated: 'A public well,' [was] to exclude [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva" - And if you say: If so, [the Mishnah] should have said "a public cistern" [bor harabbim] — and perforce a private well [would] not [be permitted], for if so, that would be [identical to the view of] Rabbi Akiva! And one can say: It is the standard way [of the Tanna] to teach [the rule] in terms of the matter that he is excluding, which is a private well [be'er hayachid]. Alternatively: That which [the Gemara] said: "[With regard to water belonging to] the public, even collected [water is permitted]," does not apply to [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, but rather to Shmuel.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:4:1.hebrew: לא שנא דרבים ולא שנא כו' - יכול להיות דהוי כר' יהודה בן בבא, והא דנקט ר' יהודה בן בבא "באר הרבים" — היינו לאפוקי בור הרבים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:4:1.english: "There is no difference whether [it is] a public [well] and no difference, etc." - It could be that [one would think] this is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava; and that which Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava stated "a public well" was [only] to exclude a public cistern.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:5:1.hebrew: שהוא ע' אמה ושיריים - וא"ת: ולילף מהר הבית, ועזרת נשים שהיה קל"ה אמה, ועזרת ישראל היה קפ"ז? וי"ל, דכל מילי דשבת ממשכן גמרינן להו. אי נמי, העזרות חשיבי מוקפין לדירה, שהיו שומרים בה כל הלילה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:5:1.english: "That is seventy cubits and a remainder" - And if you say: Let us derive [it] from the Temple Mount, and the Women's Courtyard, which was 135 cubits, and the Israelites' Courtyard, [which] was 187 [cubits]? And one can say that all matters of Shabbat we derive from the Tabernacle. Alternatively, the courtyards are considered enclosed for dwelling, since they would keep watch in them all night.

Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:5:2.hebrew: ובלבד שיהא בה שומירה - נראה לפרש, דפחות מע' אמה נמי צריך שומירה או בית דירה, וביתר מבית סאתים לא סגי בשומירה ובית דירה, אלא פתח ולבסוף הוקף הקרפף לצורך הבית. אבל אין לומר דבשבעים אמה דוקא צריך שומירה, אבל בפחות א"צ כלום, וביתר אין סגי בשומירה — דאין סברא שיהא ג' חלוקים בג' משהויין. והא נמי אין לומר, דביתר מע' נמי סגי בשומירה, ולא אתא למימר אלא דבציר משבעים אמה ושיריים לא צריך כלל — דאם כן, במאי פליג ר' עקיבא לפירוש ר"ח, דפירש דר' יהודה בן בבא איירי בדבר מועט ור' עקיבא לא איירי? דלתרוייהו בע' אמה ושיריים ודבר מועט צריך שומירה, ובפחות מכאן לא צריך! ואפי' לפי' רש"י, דפי' "היינו תנא קמא" — ד"אמרו לו לר' יהודה", מ"מ גם לפי' נראה דרבי יהודה בן בבא נמי אית ליה דבר מועט כמו תנא קמא, דמשום הכי איצטריך לרבי עקיבא לחזור ולשנות "ובלבד שיהא בה ע' אמה" כו'. ועוד, אי ביתר מבית סאתים נמי איירי ר"י בן בבא, א"כ היכי קאמר ר"י: "אפילו אין בה אלא בור ושיח ומערה"? משמע דלר"י נמי אין חילוק בין סאתים ליתר; ורבי יהודה גופיה קאמר לעיל גבי פסין "עד בית סאתים"! ועוד, לר"ח דפי' "היינו תנא קמא" — היינו ר"י בן בבא, כלומר: ואמאי הוצרך לשנות "ובלבד" כו', כיון דקאי ארבי יהודה בן בבא? והא אצטריך, דלא נימא דשרי אפילו ביתר מבית סאתים, כיון דר' יהודה בן בבא איירי ביתר מבית סאתים! לכך נראה כדפרישית. ומה שפירש רש"י: אפילו בהוקף לדירה לא שרי רבי יהודה בן בבא ביתר מבית סאתים — אין נראה, אלא בפתח ולבסוף הוקף מהני אפי' ביתר מבית סאתים; דהא שרו רבנן לעיל בדיר וסהר ומוקצה אפי' בי' כורים, וכמה חצירות ומבואות שהיו בירושלים יתרות על בית סאתים — וכי יאסור ר' יהודה בן בבא בכולם לטלטל?! ודווקא בשומירה הוא דקאמר דלא מהני ביתר מבית סאתים, אבל פתח ולבסוף הוקף מהני אפי' יותר. ולרש"י, שמא יש לחלק: דבדיר וסהר ומוקצה וחצר, לפי שתשמישתן רב יותר — אפי' י' כורין; אבל קרפף, אפי' פתח ולבסוף הוקף לא מהני ביתר מבית סאתים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 23a:5:2.english: "Provided that it contains a watchman’s booth" - It appears [correct] to explain that [an area of] less than seventy cubits [and a remainder] also requires a watchman’s booth or a dwelling place [in order to permit carrying within it], and for [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim, a watchman’s booth or a dwelling place does not suffice, but rather [only if] one opened [a door from a house into it] and subsequently enclosed the karpef for the purpose of the house. However, one cannot say that specifically at seventy cubits [and a remainder] it requires a watchman’s booth, but for less [than that] nothing is required, and for greater [than that] a watchman’s booth does not suffice — for it is unreasonable that there should be three distinct categories [differing only] by three infinitesimal amounts. And this, too, cannot be said: that for [an area] greater than seventy [cubits], a watchman’s booth also suffices, and [Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava] came to say only that for less than seventy cubits and a remainder, [a watchman’s booth] is not needed at all — for if so, in what does Rabbi Akiva disagree according to the interpretation of Rabbeinu Chananel, who explained that Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava deals with a tiny amount [in addition to seventy cubits and a remainder] and Rabbi Akiva does not deal with [it]? For according to both of them, at seventy cubits and a remainder and a tiny amount it requires a watchman’s booth, and at less than this it does not require [one]! And even according to the explanation of Rashi, who explained that "the first tanna" [in the Gemara’s question] means [the Rabbis who] "said to Rabbi Yehuda," nevertheless, according to his explanation as well, it appears that Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava also accepts [the measure of] a tiny amount, like the first tanna; for that is why it was necessary for Rabbi Akiva to go back and teach: "Provided that it measures seventy cubits [and a remainder]," etc. And furthermore, if Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava is dealing with [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim as well, if so, how could Rabbi Yehuda say: "Even if it contains only a cistern, an elongated ditch, or a cave [one may carry inside it]"? This would imply that according to Rabbi Yehuda, too, there is no difference between [an area of] two se'ah and greater [than two se'ah]; yet Rabbi Yehuda himself said above (17b) regarding the upright boards [around a well, that one may enclose only] "up to a beit se’ataim"! And furthermore, according to Rabbeinu Chananel who explained that "the first tanna" is Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava — that is: why was it necessary [for Rabbi Akiva] to teach "provided that [it measures seventy cubits and a remainder]," etc., since he is addressing Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava? But surely this was necessary, so that we should not say that it is permitted even in [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim, since Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava [allegedly] dealt with greater than a beit se’ataim! Therefore, it appears as I explained. And that which Rashi explained, that even if it was enclosed for the purpose of a dwelling, Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava does not permit [carrying] in [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim, does not appear [correct]; rather, where one opened [a door to a house] and subsequently enclosed [the area], it is effective even in [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim. For surely the Rabbis permitted above (16b) in the case of a cattle pen, a fold, and a backyard even up to ten kor! And how many courtyards and alleyways in Jerusalem were larger than a beit se’ataim — would Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava really forbid carrying in all of them?! And it is specifically regarding a watchman’s booth that he said that it is not effective in [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim, but where one opened and subsequently enclosed, it is effective even for [an area] greater [than that]. And according to Rashi, perhaps one can distinguish: that in the case of a cattle pen, a fold, a backyard, and a courtyard, because their use is more extensive, [carrying is permitted] even up to ten kor; but for a karpef, even if one opened and subsequently enclosed, it is not effective in [an area] greater than a beit se’ataim.
